body.p: Earlier there was Nurgowul, another one was Uron. Uron had many camps. Nurgowul came there. Then one of them said: "Let's shoot [at each other]". Nurgowul killed a man of Uron's. Uron ran off; [Nurgowul] shot at [him] crossing a river, he wounded his leg. He wounded him and took away his wife. Nurgowul's son was hid by the grandfather, the little one. He raised [GVY:] Most probably, there is a mistake: not Nurgowul's son, but Uron's. him for eight years. Having raised him for eight years, he began to teach him [to dodge arrows], he made a wooden arrow, then he placed him on the other side of the fire and taught. There he didn't hit, he [placed] him further away and taught again. Then he placed him very far away and taught with an iron arrow. The child was not hit by the arrow, it jumped [aside]. The ninth year came. When the ninth year came, the child found a mark on a tree, it asked the grandfather: "Who has marked it?" "I don't know". "Grandfather, please, promise, tell me". Thrice he asked his grandfather. His grandfather said: "Hunt an animal for food, then I say". There the child killed many powerful animals. After it had hunted, [the grandfather] said: "Nurgowul killed your father". "What a strong man, maybe I will grow, you, old man, tell, you'll tell, when I haven grown up". Then the child went off. It found nine yurts. Having found them it entered one big yurt. When it entered, its mother recognized [it]. "Whose child are you?", the mother said. [GVY:] Ð²ihindÄ -- probably a misprint instead of Ð²ihindÃ¤. "I don't know who it was." "How he is resembling my son!" There her son said: "That's me". "When my husband comes, don't tell", his mother said. The child said: "When will the old man come?" "He'll come in the evening." "Give me meat! I am very hungry, I was going for a long time." "He will count his meat, he will notice, shall I give it or not?" She gave [him] a bit of meat from the foot. Having swallowed it he stopped. In the evening the old man came. He counted [the meat] on the hanging racks not entering the yurt. Having counted he said: "The meat from the foot is not there". Having counted, he entered the yurt and said: "What child has come there? To whom did you give meat? Did you give it to a stranger, or to that one?" His wife said: "I gave it to that one, he ate it". "What child has come? Feed it more, it's apparently an orphan. Stir blood in the kettle for that it boils". There [the boy] got angry, having got angry he said: "You did kill my father?" "What was your father's name? Do you know my name? How is your father's name? You know my name apparently?" "I know." "[What's] my name, if you know it?" "Your name is Nurgowul." He jumped through the smoke hole behind the tent covering. [Nurgowul] did not make it [to hit] the jumping one with his knife. Then, when that one was running off, he lost [him]; he came, he put on other clothes. When he came to nine yurts: "How many are you, kill nine yurts". All were happy, they did not hit. "Well, let me shoot then", [Nurgowul] said, "dogde, jump!" With every arrow he killed. One person was left behind, a strong man was left behind. "I will kill [you] like you did kill my father." He shot into his shank, he killed him. He killed [him] and took along his mother. The grandfather said: "Now you are strong".
